result.summary:
I decided all 33 places from enlarged crops of the TIF masters. My crops and helper scripts are in scratchpad/wf3/bas-a-A/.

The clearest decisions:
- The printed misspelling περωχὴ (24.18).
- ὀνομάσοι (24.5): its tall C-shaped σ enclosing an ο is identical to the σο ligature of τοσούτου.
- μὲν in 25.17: uncial Μ with a small ε above it.
- τῆς in 26.8: the same abbreviation sign as at 24.13 and 25.21.
- Γ-shaped gamma in διεζευγμένη (25.9), confirmed by the same gamma in φθόγ (27.23).
- ἑξκαιδέκατον (26.16) and ὀκτωτέταρτον (25.25).
- Hyphen or no hyphen at the line ends of 24.22, 24.25 and 27.23.

Less certain:
- 27.13 (δὲ) and 27.24 (χορδῶν): I chose reading 1. I first took the δ form here for the δι ligature. On comparison, a δ whose stem arches over and comes straight down to the baseline also appears where no ι is possible (ὁδεύοντα, διοδεύον). The true δι ligature has a spurred ι.
- 24.23: a special δ-sort with a grave-like stroke, read as the δὲ abbreviation.
- 26.2: the grave slants only slightly.
- 27.2: a tall ει ligature, not an α.
- 25.4: left unclear. The acute sits over the ν, about equally far from α and ο, with only a slight lean toward ά.

result.summary:
I decided all 32 places from enlarged crops of the H images (ff. 64r–66v). Crops are in the h-a-A working folder. Key palaeographic calibrations behind the decisions:

- **εὐ ligature:** small loop, rising diagonal, then a υ cup. It recurs in εὖ (64r.16), εὔχρηστος (64v.15), εὐθεῖαν (65v.5), διοδεῦον (66v.6) and πλευρὰν (66r.3), and is distinct from the αὐ of αὐτο-.
- **λ:** written as a long stroke descending to the lower left; ν is μ-shaped. So V- or y-shaped descenders are γ.
- **Iota adscript:** a short mid-height vertical stroke; points are round dots.
- **α vs αι:** final α joins its stem at the bottom; αι ends in a stroke with a foot turning right.
- **Accents:** the circumflex is a thick blob with a tail curving down to the right; the grave is a thin straight stroke.

Places where neither reading is right:
- **65r.14:** διϊστάμενο(ς). The ο is written as a superscript; ς is supplied.
- **65r.19:** τοὶς ἀριθμοὶς, with written graves. The image shows ὕλη γε πομ(έν)η: γ as in γεωμετρικῶς, μ with a superscript η, and no β.

Uncertain places worth a human look:
- **64v.20:** the μόν + sign, possibly the -ος compendium.
- **65r.21:** the group between μ and ρ, which looks like the εὐ ligature; reading 2 marks ο̣ι̣ as doubtful.
- **66r.22:** ὁδεύοντα vs ὁδεύονται.

64v.9: διὰ πασῶν is marked as convention, but a grave is written over διὰ.

I decided all 32 places from enlarged crops of the H images; there were no .tif masters. Some letter forms recur in this hand and settle several places. β is written as a u-shape, as in βούλοιτο on 66r.10. λ is often a single stroke slanting down to the left, as in ὅλως, ἀλλὰ and ἄλλως on 64v.13. γ is a V whose point sits below the line. ε often joins the next letter as a small loop with a tall rising stroke, giving ευ (εὖ 64r.16, εὔχρηστος 64v.15, πλευρὰν 66r.3) and ει (μετειληφὼς 66r.3, εὐθείαν 65v.5). μ and ν look almost the same: a u-shape with a left descender. The circumflex is an arch; the grave is a straight stroke. A short upright stroke after ω is an iota adscript (τῶι 66r.12, λόγωι 66r.22); points are round dots.
On these grounds reading 1 is right at 64r.10, 64r.16 (εὖ τε (καὶ): the S-shaped καί sign, not ξ), 64v.1, 64v.13 (ὅλως), 65r.13, 65v.14, 66r.7, 66r.11 (ψη) and 66v.9 λέγεται. Reading 1 is also right at most of 66r.22: ὁδεύοντα, ἃ τῶ μὲν, with no υ and no second ν.

result.summary:
I decided all 40 places from enlarged PIL crops. Crops are in scratchpad/wf3/h-b-A/.

Several hand-specific features drove the decisions:
1. The 7-shaped sign with a grave (67r.3, 69r.3, 69v.4) is the γάρ compendium, not δ'.
2. εσ is a 6-shaped ligature. So the image gives ἀνέσεσι (67r.10), and line-end τεσ followed by a single σ in σάρων (67v.4/5, 69r.17/18, 69v.6/7).
3. In ligature, λ is written as a long slanting stroke descending below the line. So 69r.2 reads μέλος and 69v.16 reads πάλιν (with a majuscule-N ν, not η).
4. The hand uses the same μ-shaped glyph for μ and ν. I therefore marked 68v.10 (ἐμμέσω or ἐν μέσω) unclear. 69r.1 is (ἁρμο)νία, decided from the line before; only one σ is written.

Where neither reading matches the image:
- 68r.10 reads λοιποὶς.
- 69r.8 reads διό, with an acute.

Other points:
- 68r.7 is clearly τοιγαροῦν, with the γ in Γ-form.
- 68v.2 is ἰσχύν.
- The breathing on 68v.3 is smooth (ἐκκαι-).
- I chose the reading with a capital for the red majuscule initials Τ/Γ (67v.15, 68r.2, 68r.17); case could be treated as convention.
- διαπασῶν / διατεσ word-division differences are answered as convention. The MS writes διὰ with a grave in each case.

I decided all 40 places from enlarged crops of ff. 67r-70r. My crops and notes are in scratchpad/wf3/h-b-B/ (notes.txt and crops/). Neither reading wins most places; the right one changes from place to place.

Points where neither reading is right or the image cannot decide:
- 68r.10, last word: neither reading fits. After ἐξ the scribe wrote the ει ligature with an acute, the same form as in ρει on 67r.5, so the word is ἐξείρην|ται. It is neither ἐξήρην nor ἐξάρην.
- 68v.10, ἐμμέσω or ἐν μέσω: unclear. The two letters after ἐ have the same μ-like shape, and this scribe uses that shape for ν as well as μ.
- 69r.1: I chose νία. The first letter is the same μ-like shape, but the previous page ends ἁρμο-, which needs ν. Only one σ is written, so not μίας.

Points where one reading is clearly wrong (high confidence):
- 68r.7: τοιγαροῦν is right; the alternative τοιιδροῶν is wrong.
- 68r.10: λοιποὺς and νοήσομεν are right.
- 68v.2: ἰσχύν and συνέ are right.
- 69r.2: μέλος (written with λ, not ρ).
- 69r.3: προφέρεται and οὐ γ(ὰρ).
- 69r.17: κεκραμένον (the letter is α, not ω).
- 70r.3: μεταβάσεσι. Only two letters (β and ά) stand between μετα and σεσι, so μετακινήσεσι does not fit.
- 67r.3 and 69v.4: γ(ὰρ), not δ’.
- 67v.21: a small τ is written between the lines, so τ(ῆς) must stay.
- 68v.11: the line ends διαστήμα. Reading 1 writes διαστήματα here and also τα at the start of line 12, so τα appears twice.

decisions.seen: Above Η are two separate small marks. On the left is a breathing whose tail ends at the lower left, a ')' shape like the smooth breathing on εἰ in 26r.11 and unlike the '(' shaped rough breathing on ἁρμονικὸν in 26r.13. On the right is a short stroke slanting down to the right (grave). Breathing plus accent means it is not the unaccented article ἡ.
Same marks: smooth breathing plus grave, i.e. ἢ (particle).

verdicts.note: A comma-like mark stands right before ἢ, after μᾶλλον. It may be a second comma, where Basel prints an asterisk. Neither reading includes it.

verdicts.my_reading: ἑκάστῳ παιήων· ὑμέναιος· ἐξόδιος·

decisions.seen: π α ι, then η with acute, then ω and ν. These are six clear letters with no ά; the word is followed by a raised point.

verdicts.my_reading: ἄν ποτε γένοιτο· κἂν τεχνητὸν εἴη

decisions.seen: After τεχν comes the h-shaped minuscule η, then a tall Ͳ-shaped τ and ὸν with grave. There is no ι+κ sequence; κ in this hand is the ϰ-shape seen in κἂν just before.

verdicts.my_reading: ἑαυτοῦ τε καὶ τοῦ παντὸς ὀνομάσοι.

decisions.seen: After ὀνομά the sigma is the flat (horizontal) σ: a long stroke drawn along the baseline from the α to the right, turning up at its end, with οι written above it. The same flat σ appears under αὐτοσύμμε- in 75v.3. This scribe's ζ (βιαζόμενον 75v.10, χαρίζο- 75v.17) is a 2/ζ-shape with a tail descending well below the line, and nothing like that is here.

verdicts.my_reading: οὐδ᾽ ἂν φθόγγος ὅλως καλοῖτο· ἀλλὰ

decisions.seen: The letter after ὅ is closed at the top (an apex), with two legs spreading below. The left leg runs down-left below the line and the right leg joins ω. This is the same structure as λ in καλοῖτο in the same line. The scribe's μ (μὴ in 76r.11, ἐναρμόνιος in 76r.12) is open at the top (u-shaped with a left descender). The acute of ὅ sits over this letter.

verdicts.my_reading: διπλῆν ἔχον ἐπὶ τὸ ὀξὺ ...

decisions.seen: After πλ (λ is an oblique stroke falling from the π bar to below the line) come four strokes joined at the baseline: a tall stroke rising above x-height, then three short stems, with a circumflex over the 2nd and 3rd. This is exactly the pattern of ὴν in ἀρχὴν (76v.9): h-shaped η followed by ν, with the accent placed in the same way. The scribe's ω (ἔχων 76v.19) starts with a rounded bowl and has no ascender. At low magnification the group looks like 'lῶ', which explains the alternative reading.

verdicts.my_reading: μίον καὶ ἡ δίεσις καθ᾽ ἑαυτὰ θεωρού-

decisions.seen: After ἑαυτ the final letter is α: the same open 'a' form as the α of ἑα- at the start of the word, linked to θ. It carries a grave. It is not the small closed ο of θεωρού-.

verdicts.my_reading: μεῖν ἠπίως πῶς καὶ εὐρύθμως

decisions.seen: An arched circumflex stroke is clearly written above the ω of π-ω-σ, so the scribe wrote πῶς with an accent.

After καὶ: a smooth breathing, then a looped ε (tall stroke ending in a loop), from which a cup-shaped stroke (υ) sweeps along the baseline and rises into a single ρ with a long descender, then ϋ with acute, θ, μ, ω, ς. Only one ρ is present: the cup stroke has neither bowl nor descender, so it cannot be a second ρ.

verdicts.note: πῶς with a circumflex (not enclitic πως) is the scribe's accentuation.

verdicts.my_reading: ἣν ἔχει πρὸς τοὺς αὐτοῦ

decisions.seen: First word: a tall stroke plus three short stems joined at the baseline (h-shaped η + ν). It is identical in form to χὴν directly above, at the start of 80r.11. Above it are a small rough breathing and a straight grave stroke; the curved stroke higher up is the end of χ from line 11. There is no ω of the closed ꙍ type this hand uses on this page (τῶν 80r.11, ἔχων 80r.10) and no circumflex.

verdicts.my_reading: λόγον ἡμιόλιον | ἔχων, ...

decisions.seen: After χ is a large closed loop with an inner stroke, the scribe's ω form (the same as in τῶν in 80r.11). It is about twice the size of ο, and ν follows.

verdicts.my_reading: [ἐ]πὶ δὲ τῶν ἐμπνευστῶν

decisions.seen: The first glyph is π (a long top bar over two legs), followed by ι with diaeresis and a grave. There is no τ, no η, and no circumflex or iota subscript.

The left margin at line 10, where outdented initials stand, is blank. Sections on this page begin with an outdented red initial (red Τ at 80v.2), and here the text starts at the normal margin with πὶ, so the initial ε was never written. δὲ itself is identical in both readings.

verdicts.my_reading: ἢ ἁρμονία συνέχεται τὸ ἁρμονικὸν

decisions.seen: Above η: a crescent ')' breathing (smooth) to the left and a long grave stroke. The rough breathings on ἁρμονία and ἁρμονικὸν in the same line are angular L-shaped, which is different.
Smooth breathing plus grave on η = ἢ (particle).

verdicts.my_reading: λαμβανόμενον ἀπαρτίζεται μέλος·

decisions.seen: ἀ with smooth breathing, then the long-barred π, α, ρ, τί, ζ, εται. There is no κ and no κατ- before αρτ.

verdicts.my_reading: μονίας προφέρεται· οὐδὲ διὰ ...

decisions.seen: After the barred π: a loop whose tail sweeps under the line to the right into a second loop (the ρ+ο ligature), then φέρεται. This is identical to πρὸς at 80r.12 in the same hand. περι- in this hand (περιέχον 80v.15) is written π-ε-ρ-ϊ with separate ε and ι, which is not the case here.
Same: no ε and no ι between π and φ, only the ρο ligature.

verdicts.my_reading: ἀπήρτισται· δύο δὲ τόνοις καὶ ἡ-

decisions.seen: After τί, under a long bar, a closed loop is joined at its foot to a stem with a small hook. This is the στ ligature, followed by α and ι with descender. Compare the plain τ (bar and stem, no loop) in -πται at the end of 81v.9.

verdicts.my_reading: μιτονίῳ διείρηπται· δύο τονιαί-

decisions.seen: After ει (acute above): a filled bowl at x-height with a long straight descender running down-left well below the line, and no ascender. This matches the ρ of ἀπήρτισται (81v.8). λ in this hand (λαμβανόμενον, μέλος 81v.2) is an inverted V with a rising top stroke, standing on the line.

verdicts.note: ρ for λ appears to be a slip by the scribe; Basel has διείληπται.

verdicts.my_reading: τετραχόρδου περὶ τὰ διαστήματα τοῦ

decisions.seen: τὰ: tall τ followed by an open α (not a small closed ο), with a grave above.
The acute stands over η of διαστη-. There is no accent over the α of δια-.
After διαστή the word continues μ-α-τ-α (-ματα) and then Τοῦ; it does not end in -μα.
